title: Hanuman Chalisa: An Astronomical Viewpoint
sub: Notes on this standalone talk by Brajesh Gautam, The Anchor Of Life: why Hanuman never arrives without Ram, the navel as the seat of Hanuman consciousness, the Ramayana read as an inner allegory, Mars exalted in Capricorn, Ketu and Rahu in the body, and mangal dosha remedies.
desc: Complete notes on Hanuman Chalisa: An Astronomical Viewpoint by Brajesh Gautam: the navel as Hanuman's seat, chakras mapped to the zodiac, Mars exalted in Capricorn, the Ramayana as an inner allegory of Ram, Sita, Lakshman and Ravana, Ketu and Rahu in the body, and mangal dosha remedies, with video timestamps.
points: Every other deity in his list has a consort; Hanuman holds his own power, but the speaker says that power only moves in service of Ram and Sita.
The navel, not the head, is called the seat of Hanuman.
He places the first chakra to form, and the one that directs 72,000 nadis, at the navel, not at the crown or the brow.
Mars exalted in Capricorn is read as Hanuman at full power.
That placement sits, in his scheme, at the root chakra, lighting up Saturn's usual darkness.
The Ramayana is read as one person's inner story.
Ram is the larger awareness, Sita the individual self, Lakshman is discernment, Ravana is ego, and Hanuman is the life-breath that burns the ego away.
Ketu and Rahu are read onto the body itself.
Anything that sticks out, a tail, an ear, hair, a beard, is folded into this scheme, with claimed effects on health and temperament that these notes do not endorse.
Mangal dosha gets specific, named household remedies.
A red cow fed jaggery, seven cowries in red cloth, and monkey figures placed to the south, each tied to a different named problem.
